channel.title: Nature Physics
channel.description: Nature Physics offers news and reviews alongside top-quality research papers in a monthly publication, covering the entire spectrum of physics. Physics addresses the properties and interactions of matter and energy, and plays a key role in the development of a broad range of technologies. To reflect this, Nature Physics covers all areas of pure and applied physics research. The journal focuses on core physics disciplines, but is also open to a broad range of topics whose central theme falls within the bounds of physics.

item.title: [8] Spinon mediation of witness spin dynamics in herbertsmithite
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Felix Flicker, J. C. Séamus Davis

Authors: Hiroto Takahashi, Jack Murphy, Mitikorn Wood-Thanan, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important experimental study of spinon dynamics in the iconic kagome lattice spin liquid candidate herbertsmithite.

Tags: #experiment #herbertsmithite #spinliquid #kagomelattice

Abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 10 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03303-6 There is a long-running effort to find a material with a spin liquid ground state, but existing experimental probes have not given definitive evidence. Now, impurity spins have been used as probes of the putative spin liquid phase of herbertsmithite.

item.title: [8] Bilayer excitons in the Laughlin fractional quantum Hall state
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: D. E. Feldman, J. I. A. Li

Authors: Ron Q. Nguyen, Naiyuan J. Zhang, Navketan Khurana-Batra, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: High-impact experiment on fractional quantum Hall states and excitons in a graphene device.

Tags: #experiment #graphene #fractionalquantumHall #excitons

Abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 09 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03325-0 Laughlin states are descriptions of the quantum Hall effect in which interactions between electrons create fractionally charged quasiparticles. Now, excitons are shown to form between these quasiparticles in a bilayer graphene device.

item.title: [8] Superconductivity on two surfaces
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Tingxin Li

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Observation of unconventional superconductivity in rhombohedral multilayer graphene, relevant to moire and 2D materials.

Tags: #experiment #graphene #superconductivity #multilayergraphene

Abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 05 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03290-8 In rhombohedral multilayer graphene, superconductivity emerges from an unusual normal state in which electrons and holes reside on opposite surfaces of the crystal.
